reason: A ~60-70-person NYC fintech ($26M raised, MissionOG/Third Prime) is hiring its first Applied AI Lead to 'own the AI layer powering our internal operations' and 'serve as the technical guardrail for AI work happening across the company' - the exact AI-in-operations plus verification-capacity problem Daniel ran at Tricentis, in his deepest vertical (payments).

company.name: Alternative Payments
company.one_liner: B2B payments and AR/AP automation platform - the 'financial operating system' for service-based SMBs, starting with managed service providers (MSPs).
company.stage: Growth startup, founded 2021; $22M announced Apr 2025 (led by MissionOG and Third Prime), ~$26M total; ~60-70 employees
company.hq: New York, NY (with presence in Canada, Brazil, UK)

evidence_jobs.title: Applied AI Lead
evidence_jobs.quote: You'll work alongside our bizops, finance, support and engineering teams to identify where AI can eliminate manual work, reduce cycle time and surface better decisions. You'll also serve as the technical guardrail for AI work happening across the company, setting the architecture, security standards and integration patterns that let teams build with confidence.

evidence_jobs.title: Head of Product
evidence_jobs.quote: We're at an inflection point: closing the loop on money movement and laying the foundation for a platform that will reshape how service businesses operate financially.

evidence_jobs.title: Lead Software Engineer
evidence_jobs.quote: We're looking for a Lead Software Engineer who's as comfortable talking about how a business makes money as they are designing a distributed system.

people_spec: Chief Operating Officer - owns the Applied AI Lead search and the internal-operations cost problem it is meant to solve; primary buyer
CEO & Founder - founder-led company, sets the platform/AI bet at the inflection point
VP of Engineering (co-founder, founding engineer) - owns the platform and would own the guardrail architecture; note there is no separately verifiable CTO, so this is the top technical seat
Head of Product (currently an open role, so no incumbent to route through)
Head of Data (currently an open role - the analytics half of the same bet)
talk_track: I spent the last year at Tricentis putting AI agents into production for incident detection and on-call response, and before that ran platform engineering at Ripple and PayPal - the work was always making cost-to-deliver stop scaling one-for-one with headcount. Your Applied AI Lead posting asks one person to both "identify where AI can eliminate manual work, reduce cycle time" and "serve as the technical guardrail for AI work happening across the company." Those are two different jobs, and in my experience companies staff the first one and discover the second about six months in, after a few agents are already load-bearing in finance and support. The guardrail half - evaluation harnesses, data access controls, integration patterns - is cheap to build before the first agent ships and expensive to retrofit after. Read against the same posting's line about being "at an inflection point," the number that quietly decides the next round is cost-to-serve per MSP staying flat while AP and analytics revenue grows. Is the guardrail layer getting designed before or after the first agents ship? - Daniel Kirichanski, Prime Path Global
